meta.title: Icelandic Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 734 expressions · 109 everyday, 156 fixed, 336 particle verbs, 102 idioms, 31 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 734 Icelandic set phrases, fixed expressions, particle verbs, idioms and proverbs, in five subdecks: 109 everyday phrases, 156 fixed expressions, 336 particle verbs, 102 idioms and 31 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Icelandic → English (see the Icelandic, recall the meaning) and English → Icelandic (see an English meaning, recall the Icelandic) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Icelandic A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas (má ég, hvar er, ég skil ekki …). The FIXED EXPRESSIONS are the multi-word adverbs, prepositions and conjunctions sentences are built from (af hverju, eins og, undir eins …). The PARTICLE VERBS are a verb and a particle or a preposition that together mean something the verb alone does not (fara í, vera með, kunna að …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (sem stendur, taka þátt, allt í einu …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (allt er gott sem endar vel, brennt barn forðast eldinn, ekki er allt gull sem glóir …). Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Icelandic sentences contain them, a particle verb being counted with its verb in any form; 200 of the 734 are found there, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. The deck takes every expression English Wiktionary lists for Icelandic that passes its filters, rather than the commonest of many. Real example sentences come with 197 of the 734 expressions, three apiece for 98, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). The forms of a particle verb's verb, used to find it in a sentence: The Database of Icelandic Morphology (Beygingarlýsing íslensks nútímamáls). The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies. Author and editor Kristín Bjarnadóttir. https://bin.arnastofnun.is (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
